executive_summary.insight: Big Tech engineering supply is at a multi-year high — Oracle's 30,000-person cut is the single largest of 2026, alongside Amazon's 16,000+ and Google's diffuse, unannounced rolling cuts.
executive_summary.action: Run a dedicated sourcing sprint against platform, infra and cloud engineers now, while the pool is fresh and less contested.

executive_summary.insight: Fintech peers are diverging: Stripe and Salesforce are still net-hiring engineers even as they trim support and ops roles, while PayPal keeps shrinking.
executive_summary.action: Expect stronger counteroffers on senior fintech engineering candidates — Stripe is actively competing for the same profiles, including in Bengaluru.

executive_summary.insight: Microsoft's voluntary buyout and Uber's delayering are releasing senior engineering and product leaders, but Meta's Reality Labs cut is the only notable Tier 1/2 release on the design side.
executive_summary.action: Prioritize engineering and product sourcing now; treat design as a slower-burn search and warm passive candidates instead.

executive_summary.insight: Intuit's own Bangalore openings skew heavily toward Software Engineering (10 of 30 roles), with AI, ML and finance-systems skill needs, and only one open Product Management role.
executive_summary.action: Match sourcing effort to this mix — most of the near-term hiring pressure is on engineering, not product or design.

executive_summary.insight: Design hiring demand from Tier 1/2 companies is currently thin, while engineering supply from the same companies is unusually deep.
executive_summary.action: Rebalance recruiter time toward engineering pipelines this cycle; keep design sourcing lightweight until a clearer signal appears.

market_reads.label: Hire now
market_reads.rationale: Oracle's 30,000-person cut, Amazon's 16,000+ reductions and Google's ongoing rolling cuts have put an unusually large pool of senior Big Tech engineers on the market at the same time — the deepest engineering supply in recent years. This favors moving now on Intuit's 10 open Bangalore engineering roles, several of which are AI/ML and platform-focused.

market_reads.label: Selective
market_reads.rationale: Supply is uneven across Tier 2 companies: Uber's delayering and Salesforce's ongoing product-management reductions are releasing experienced PMs, but Stripe is still net-hiring aggressively for the same profiles, so expect stronger competition there. Salesforce's recent cuts are the closer skill match for Intuit's open Staff PM – Finance Systems role.

market_reads.label: Wait & build pipeline
market_reads.rationale: Design supply from Tier 1/2 companies is thin right now — Meta's Reality Labs cut is the only notable release, and it's weighted toward AR/hardware rather than product design. Expect a longer search for Intuit's Senior Product Designer – AI Interaction role; use this window to warm passive candidates rather than expecting a fast influx.

talent_insights.supply_pocket: Senior and staff-level Big Tech engineering (Oracle, Amazon, Google) is the single largest available talent pool this quarter — larger than anything currently visible on the product or design side.
talent_insights.wait_signal: Microsoft's voluntary buyout was announced but hasn't fully played out yet. Expect a second wave of senior engineering and product leaders to actually reach the open market over the next 60–90 days as separations finalize, so this pool isn't fully visible yet.

targets.intuit_role: Staff/Senior/Principal Software Engineer & Staff ML Engineer (AI, Finance Systems, Business Intelligence)
targets.why: Largest, most recent cuts in cloud, database and AI infrastructure engineering — the closest skill match to Intuit's open AI-native-builder and ML engineer roles.
Recent rounds specifically hit product management and enterprise/finance-adjacent teams — a closer match than Uber's more consumer-facing PM profile.

targets.intuit_role: Senior Product Designer – AI Interaction Design
targets.why: The only Tier 1/2 company with a recent design-adjacent release; treat this as a small, specific pool rather than a broad supply signal.
The voluntary buyout program specifically targets senior-director level and below, making it the most directly comparable pool for this level.

talent_insights.intuit_context: Intuit's Bangalore office currently lists about 30 open roles: Software Engineering is the largest category (10 roles), followed by Finance (8), Data (3), Program Management and Security/Risk/Fraud (2 each), and one each in Product Management and Information Technology.

signals.headline: Oracle cuts roughly 30,000 roles, the year's largest reduction
signals.summary: Oracle eliminated an estimated 30,000 positions to help fund its expanding AI infrastructure spend, making it the single deepest cut of 2026 across tech.
signals.recommendation: Worth a dedicated sourcing sprint given the scale — particularly for cloud and database infrastructure engineers.

signals.headline: Amazon passes 16,000 cuts through Q1, concentrated in AWS and corporate roles
signals.summary: Amazon's reductions spread across roughly 90 days rather than one announcement, driven by delayering under Andy Jassy's ownership push and a product-strategy shift in some engineering teams. Capex toward AWS data centers and AI chips continues to rise.
signals.recommendation: The effective sourcing window is about 90 days post-separation — prioritize outreach to recent cohorts over older ones.

signals.headline: Google's engineering cuts stay diffuse — no single headline number
signals.summary: An estimated 1,500 to 3,000+ engineers have been displaced through rolling performance cuts, Platform & Devices restructuring (Android, Chrome, Pixel) and manager delayering, spread across several unrelated programs.
signals.recommendation: Because there's no single WARN filing to react to, source proactively — target Android/Chrome/Platform alumni directly rather than waiting for a layoff list.

signals.headline: Meta to cut ~10% of Reality Labs, about 1,000 roles
signals.summary: Meta plans to reduce its Reality Labs division, which employs roughly 15,000 people, as the company reallocates focus and spending toward AI.
signals.recommendation: AR/VR-adjacent engineers and hardware/product designers are newly available — useful if you have any spatial or advanced-interface initiatives, otherwise a general signal of strong passive senior talent in market.

signals.headline: Microsoft offers first-ever buyout to up to 7% of staff
signals.summary: The one-time voluntary retirement program targets senior-director-level employees and below whose combined age and tenure reach 70, part of a broader restructuring wave at the company.
signals.recommendation: Buyouts like this tend to release experienced director-level engineering and product leaders who may be open to a smaller, more agile team — worth direct outreach.

signals.headline: Uber to cut about 10% of its workforce, ~3,400 roles
signals.summary: Uber is removing management layers and simplifying team structures as part of a broader effort to refocus investment on its biggest opportunities.
signals.recommendation: Flattening of management layers typically frees up mid-to-senior product and platform-engineering leaders — a window to target org-design-minded PMs.

signals.headline: Salesforce keeps cutting support and ops while growing overall headcount
signals.summary: 2026 rounds hit marketing, product management, data analytics, Agentforce and MuleSoft teams, even as total headcount reached a record high and AI tools are credited with a 30%+ engineering productivity gain that's reducing new hiring needs.
signals.recommendation: A good market for experienced enterprise PMs and data analysts released in recent rounds, but expect strong counteroffers since Salesforce is still net-hiring engineers overall.

signals.headline: Stripe stays in net-hiring mode with ~500 open roles
signals.summary: Stripe has had no new layoffs in 2026 and continues hiring aggressively, weighted toward engineering, AI infrastructure and international expansion including a growing Bengaluru presence.
signals.recommendation: Expect tighter competition and faster counteroffers on fintech infrastructure and payments engineers, especially candidates open to Bengaluru.

signals.headline: PayPal continues trimming headcount at its San Jose HQ
signals.summary: A fresh round of permanent layoffs was filed with California employment regulators, continuing a pattern of year-over-year headcount decline at the company.
signals.recommendation: Monitor for payments-engineering and risk/product talent entering the market — relevant for fintech-adjacent roles.
